$comment: The ONE file in qf-atlas a human edits by hand. Everything else is generated.
Maps a finding id (from atlas.json) to what you decided about it.
Anything not listed here counts as 'undecided'.
keep      intentional, not debt
repair    real, scheduled -> becomes a work order
remove    confirmed dead -> becomes a deletion batch
accepted  known debt you are living with
ONE SCHEMA. The human field is `reason`. There is no `why` here: the analyzer also
emits a `reason` (why a finding is unresolved), and two fields spelled differently
for the same job is how half of these entries drifted out of the shape the baseline
gate reads. Required keys, by verdict:
keep                 verdict, owner, reason
repair / remove      verdict, owner, reason, remediation_trigger
accepted             verdict, owner, reason, remediation_trigger, review_or_expiry
An entry missing a required key is still a decision for counting purposes - that is
what it has always meant, and normalising a schema may not silently re-adjudicate
anything. It is reported INCOMPLETE, and completeness IS enforced where it carries
authority: baseline.mjs refuses to seed a hard red from an incomplete record, and
`accepted` without its metadata has never counted as a decision at all.
All clear means undecided == 0. It does not mean zero findings: some coverage
gaps are unparseable without a compiler, and some debt is deliberate.
Ids are semantic, so they survive edits inside a file. Renaming a file or
moving the SQL retires the old id and raises a fresh undecided one, which is
correct: code that moved deserves another look.
2026-08-17 expunge: the four remove verdicts were executed and their findings no longer exist, so their entries were pruned. The reasoning lives in the commit that deleted them.

2026-08-19 — the three governed-review hard reds are adjudicated REPAIR. No expiry: they are being repaired, not accepted. Ownership findings are deliberately NOT here: multiple structural claimants is not proof of competing ownership, so they stay amber until independently adjudicated.

2026-08-18 D6 schema migration: five entries carried `why` and were renamed to `reason` verbatim. No verdict, owner or wording changed. The three `repair` entries below with no `remediation_trigger` are INCOMPLETE and say so; inventing a trigger for them would be authoring founder intent, so they are left for the founder to fill in.

unreachable:collab-electron/src/windows/.reason: Founder-authored brand engine. qa/gates/one-skin.ts:21 allowlists this exact path as one of two justified palette exceptions, and WO-007 describes it as imported verbatim as founder input. flow-cube-watermark.js does not import it (the apparent import at line 16 is a usage comment), so 'unimported' is accurate and irrelevant: it is an asset, not dead wiring.

broken-bridge-call:ptyForegroundProcess.reason: REAL RUNTIME DEFECT in a live window. terminal IS a build input, and terminal/src/App.tsx:202 awaits window.api.ptyForegroundProcess(session.id), which neither preload exposes — it throws TypeError when that path runs. Verified pre-existing at d543b01, so atlas-strip-1 did not cause it; removing the orphaned pty:foreground-process main handler was correct. Fix is to restore the preload method or drop the call site.
